title: I2C Collision-Avoidance Robot
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning MicroPython
description: Top view of a robot driving in a rectangular arena with one VL53L0X distance sensor on the I2C bus. Within 15 cm it backs up 20 cm, flips a coin and turns left or right. Shows the I2C transaction bytes, the distance values, a chart and a log of reads, with sliders for read rate and robot speed.

educational.topic: Using an I2C distance sensor for collision avoidance
learningObjectives: Predict how the read rate and the robot speed change how close the robot gets to a wall before it reacts
Explain that the robot only knows the distance when an I2C read finishes
Read two data bytes from the sensor and turn them into millimeters and centimeters

keyQuestions: How far does the robot travel between two reads?
What happens when the read rate is too slow for the robot speed?
Is the coin flip really 50 percent each way?
commonMisconceptions: The robot sees the wall all the time (it only knows the distance when a read finishes)
A coin flip alternates left and right (each turn is an independent 50/50 chance)
assessmentOpportunities: Student predicts the bump count for new slider settings
Student decodes two data bytes into millimeters
